**Question:** What should the tool do when the program reading its output closes early — for example `python -m logredact big.log | head -5`? (FR-023, FR-024)

**Why it matters:** This is the most common way anyone will actually run the tool, and by default a Python program in this situation dumps an ugly `BrokenPipeError` traceback to standard error and exits non-zero. That would contradict the spec's promise that a successful run writes nothing to standard error — so `head` would look like a failure every time.

**Recommended:** Option A — treating a closed output pipe as normal, silent completion matches how every standard Unix filter behaves (`cat`, `grep`, `sed`), and keeps the "nothing on standard error, exit 0" contract honest for the single most common invocation.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Stop quietly as soon as the output pipe closes: no message on standard error, no traceback, no `--count` summary, exit status 0 |
| B | Stop quietly but still print the `--count` summary for the lines that were written, exit status 0 |
| C | Treat it as a failure: print a diagnostic to standard error and exit with status 2 |
| D | Leave it unspecified — out of scope for this feature |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
